title: Peddling charcoal and illegal shrimp with Danny's father
summary: He and Danny helped Chris Columbo peddle coal and wood by wagon; other peddlers sold shrimp illegally.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What's pedaling charcoal? I never have seen anybody do that. How they do it.
You've never seen charcoal and stone coal and wood?
I've seen that, but never seen it in New Orleans. I've never seen the way they pedaled it. What did they do?

Well, I don't think you'd see it now. It's such an old page of history. Well, we'd hitch the horse up to the wagon and we'd load the stone coal on the front and maybe the wood on the back or whatever he was going to pedal that thing. He had regular customers who would go to these houses and I, when I was Danny and I would get out and knock on the door and the people would come out and they'd buy whatever they wanted from Chris. That was his daddy, Chris Columbo.

Well, some peddlers used to call out their wares and they'd go through the block and hollering, well, we have, I got shrimp or I got this or I got that. And the customers would come out and purchase it from them. Well, this was a little different with Chris. He was mostly a charcoal or a stone coal or wood pedal. He would pedal.
Well, he never did yell out anything at all.

No, he didn't have to. He had his regular customs. Do you remember some of the things that the other people yelled? Could you imitate them? No, I don't believe I came out. I said, my wife, she said, lady, I got bananas, I got this, and I can't even name it, I got shrimp. And hell, he'd have the shrimp sometime when they'd be watching for the policemen. Policemen come in and he's selling shrimps. He's going to tell it because policemen are going to arrest them because it was a violation of the law to sell shrimps in the open. But they would take a chance.
And that would, I guess they were trying to keep people from getting bad seafood or something.

Right. And that was in the other days, which you can readily see that the way these things sparrow so easily. But these guys could always sell them. And then too, the license, another thing implicated that they were getting by just peddling on their own on these riders.

They should have had licenses then, but not for the open sales when it's like that. So it was a violation, but the guy made his living during that. There's always been violation of the laws down through the years.
